facts.fact: Official Korea.kr Oct 19 briefing records Lee presenting appointment certificates to seven minister-level officials and the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency chief at the presidential office. Confirms activity on that occasion only.

Constitution Art. 65 permits impeachment for official-duty constitutional/statutory violations; presidential motion needs majority proposal and two-thirds passage. Passage suspends exercise of authority pending adjudication; an impeachment decision removes the official. Art. 71 separately covers acting authority if presidency is vacant or President unable to perform duties; Art. 84 bars criminal charges during tenure except insurrection/treason. Suspension of powers is textually distinct from removal/ceasing office; whether it meets this contract’s “ceases to be President” wording remains interpretive.

Yonhap Oct. 19: Seoul Central District Prosecutors Office chief Park Chul-woo told an Assembly audit he had not considered withdrawing Lee-related indictments and would not comment on future indictment/arrest decisions. Yonhap says Lee’s multiple criminal trials are suspended under Art. 84 during his presidency. This is not removal, detention or evidence of an impeachment motion.

At an Oct. 16 parliamentary audit, Seoul High Court chief judge Kim Dae-woong said trials were suspended based on a constitutional provision; reporting says five Lee cases’ hearing dates were indefinitely postponed. Lawmakers disputed Art. 84 scope. This is firsthand audit reporting, not an inspected court order; publisher flags English as AI-translated.

KBS Oct. 16: ruling DP was discussing impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice Jo Hee-de; opposition PPP leader warned this could prompt calls for Lee’s impeachment. Immediate debate concerned Jo; no Lee motion reported. Yonhap June 4: DP won 9 of 14 Assembly by-elections and retained a majority in the 300-seat Assembly. Two-thirds passage threshold is above a simple majority; exact Oct. 19 membership not independently checked.
